label: UniFi Dream Machine Special Edition
description: Ubiquiti UDM-SE - 10G cloud gateway with NVR: 8x 1GbE RJ45 LAN (2 PoE+, 6 PoE, 180W), 1x 2.5GbE RJ45 WAN, 2x 10G SFP+.

poe.note: 180 W, from the tech-spec table row "PoE Budget = 180W" (with "PoE = 15.4W", "PoE+ = 30W", "Voltage Range PoE Mode = PoE: 44-57V / PoE+: 50-57V"), read 2026-11-19: https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-se . The same box's datasheet, https://dl.ui.com/ds/udm_se_ds.pdf (200, 358,669 B, text layer), prints the placement and per-port maxima but not the aggregate - "PoE interface (6) PoE (Pair A 1, 2+; 3, 6-) / (2) PoE+" and "Max. PoE wattage per port by PSE PoE: 15.4W / PoE+: 30W" - which is what the two PoE+ and six PoE poeOutClass values on ports 1-8 already follow. 8 ports at their class maxima is 152.4 W, inside the 180 W budget. The aggregate exists on the vendor page only; the datasheet is cited here so the placement is not read off the same table as the total.

notes:
Power: none of these copper ports accepts PoE. Vendor page https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-se (HTTP 200, 682,320 B, read 2026-11-19, server-rendered tech-spec table) says "Power Method = (1) Universal AC input, 100-240V AC, 4.4A Max., 50/60 Hz (1) USP-RPS DC input, 52V DC, 3.94A"; a box fed from mains, a USB-C supply or a DC jack has no PoE-PD front end, so WAN now declare poeIn: false. Without that declaration the engine's isPoePd() match on "unifi" gave each silent copper port a 12.95 W 802.3af draw - the defect PR #2118 and PR #2121 fixed across the UXG family (refs #130).

**LAN bank (layer 2), read 2026-11-21.** Both vendor surfaces print the same three rows: `MAC Address Table Size = 4,000`, `LACP Port Aggregation = True` with the note "GbE RJ45 ports 1-8", and `VLAN/Subnet-based Traffic Segmentation = True`, beside `1 GbE RJ45 = 8` and `2.5 GbE RJ45 = 1` (the WAN port) - https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-se (HTTP 200, 682,320 B), and the storefront's own payload repeats each row at https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/udm-se (HTTP 200, 602,395 B). A 4,000-entry MAC table is a bridge forwarding database, and a LAG over the eight 1G sockets cannot be built from routed ports, so Port 1-Port 8 forward at layer 2 and the row declares `l2-forward` (MAC learning + flooding only; VLAN, LAG and STP ride on it). Measured on the pre-change spec: hosts on Port 1 and Port 2 in 192.168.1.0/24 could not resolve each other's ARP, and `switchport access vlan 10` answered "cannot switch frames: it has no l2-forward capability". `no switchport` still makes a LAN port routed; the WAN port keeps its address. The two 10G SFP+ cages keep their addresses as well.
